html:
Wife of Augustus for more than fifty years and the most powerful woman of early imperial Rome.

She was from the old Claudian family. Her first husband was Tiberius Claudius Nero, with whom she had two sons, Tiberius and Drusus. In 38 BCE she divorced him and married Octavian, while pregnant with Drusus. She and Augustus had no children together, but the marriage lasted until his death.

Augustus trusted her advice. She ran a large household and fortune, had her own estates, among them the villa at Prima Porta where the Augustus of Prima Porta statue was found, and was held up as a model Roman wife. In his will Augustus adopted her into his family and she became Julia Augusta.

Under her son Tiberius, now emperor, she kept great influence and the two often clashed. Ancient writers, above all Tacitus, hinted that she poisoned rivals to clear the way for him; there is no proof. She died in 29 CE, and her grandson Claudius made her a goddess in 42 CE. She was the root of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.
sum: Wife of Augustus for more than fifty years and the most powerful woman of early imperial Rome.
